builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Beyond the Grid: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit for Interpretable Signal Decomposition
summary: It replaces discrete matching pursuit, sparse coding with gridded dictionaries, and opaque neural decomposers with greedy gradient-based optimization over continuous differentiable atom families (periodic, trend, transient, discontinuous). Cost is per-signal iterative optimization with data-driven priors and spectral sharpness annealing, plus a tuned atom budget and residual stopping criterion, rather than a single forward pass or one dictionary lookup. It can fail when true components lie outside the library, when greedy selection mis-isolates overlapping or nonstationary components, and when annealing, priors, or stopping thresholds are mis-set, since the 1% recovery and forecasting gains are conditional on library expressibility and evaluated workloads.
rationale: This is a specialized interpretable time-series decomposition method, not a general LLM efficiency technique, so it warrants small-scale validation only for teams whose production work involves signal decomposition or structured forecasting targets.
technique: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit for signal decomposition

claims.statement: It replaces discrete matching pursuit, sparse coding with gridded dictionaries, and opaque neural decomposers with greedy gradient-based optimization over continuous differentiable atom families (periodic, trend, transient, discontinuous). Cost is per-signal iterative optimization with data-driven priors and spectral sharpness annealing, plus a tuned atom budget and residual stopping criterion, rather than a single forward pass or one dictionary lookup. It can fail when true components lie outside the library, when greedy selection mis-isolates overlapping or nonstationary components, and when annealing, priors, or stopping thresholds are mis-set, since the 1% recovery and forecasting gains are conditional on library expressibility and evaluated workloads.

Recovers generative parameters to within 1% on stationary synthetic signals in its library; best sparsity-accuracy trade-off among classical, continuous-pursuit, and neural baselines in the sparse regime; improves forecasting accuracy on most evaluated datasets when atoms are used as curriculum targets.
